title: FEMA assistance can fund temporary housing and repairs while access and post-disaster housing remain constrained
source_unit: GAO-26-108154, a review of FEMA Individual Assistance data and 56 interviews and written responses from FEMA and state/local governments
geography: United States; Hurricanes Helene and Milton, 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, and 2025 Texas floods, with selected FEMA and state/local institutional evidence

observations.period: Recent disasters covered by FEMA data; GAO report published April 22, 2026

denominator.unit: individuals and households receiving more than $3 billion in FEMA Individual Assistance across selected recent disasters

assistance_scale.value: over $3 billion provided to 1.2 million individuals and households

eligible_uses.value: assistance can cover necessary expenses and serious needs not covered by insurance or low-interest loans, including temporary lodging, rental housing, and home repairs
eligible_uses.unit: Individual Assistance route and eligible-use description

access_barriers.value: most survivors affected by the reviewed Helene/Milton and Texas-flood events faced long helpline wait times and could not reach a representative when trying to apply

letter_interpretation.value: some survivors interpreted requests for more information as denial letters; FEMA revised letters in 2024 and 2025

housing_constraints.value: survivors and officials faced long-standing post-disaster housing constraints; destroyed pre-existing housing resources and setup requirements delayed direct housing in selected cases

delivery_change.value: FEMA shifted toward state/local centers and discontinued door-to-door canvassing, raising access concerns for older, disabled, rural, and phone/internet-limited survivors
delivery_change.unit: delivery model change and access-risk assessment

observations.method: GAO reviewed FEMA Individual Assistance data on amounts provided, helpline calls, and eligibility letters and analyzed information from 56 interviews and written responses from FEMA and state/local governments affected by recent disasters.
observations.uncertainty: The $3 billion and 1.2 million figures are agency totals across selected disasters and do not establish a survivor-level receipt, adequacy, repair, safe return, or housing-stability rate. Selected helpline, letter, and housing evidence is not a representative prevalence estimate. The report does not link a named property or survivor through application, award, payment, repair, move, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: Individuals and households affected by Hurricanes Helene and Milton, the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, and the 2025 Texas floods; older adults, people with disabilities, rural residents, and people without phone/internet access are identified as potentially affected by delivery changes; FEMA and state/local officials are separate institutional units.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate assistance can coexist with serious access barriers because totals do not reveal who was eligible, reached, paid, adequately repaired, or still housed. State/local centers may improve coordination and door-to-door work may be costly or duplicative; the access effects of the delivery change remain empirical questions.

observations.period: 2025-2026; GAO review interviews and written responses

denominator.unit: interviews and written responses from FEMA and state/local governments impacted by disasters in recent years

state_capacity.value: officials from four states affected by Helene and Milton reported that they did not have their own individual-assistance programs

federal_dependence.value: federal and state officials emphasized that state and local governments need time to prepare for changes because they currently rely on significant federal support

observations.method: GAO synthesis of interviews and written responses from FEMA and affected state/local governments; institutional evidence is retained separately from the agency assistance total.
observations.uncertainty: The selected officials and governments are not a representative sample of all jurisdictions or survivor experiences. Reported reliance and capacity do not establish the effectiveness, cost, or legitimacy of any future division of responsibilities.
observations.subgroup: FEMA and selected state/local governments affected by recent disasters, including four states without their own individual-assistance programs in the cited evidence.
observations.counterinterpretation: State/local reliance on FEMA may reflect efficient federal pooling rather than incapacity, and a transition period could improve local ownership if resources and time are adequate.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report PDF provides Individual Assistance totals, helpline and letter evidence, housing constraints, delivery changes, and interview context.
Related GAO workforce-capacity report; workforce and survivor-assistance routes are not pooled into one outcome.

boundary: This record adds an assistance-to-housing-reach and intergovernmental-capacity layer. It does not establish survivor-level eligibility, notice, application, award, payment receipt, repair completion, safe occupancy, move/stay, durable housing security, trust, or political action.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO landing page and full report PDF reviewed; underlying FEMA administrative data and interview materials are not retained.
